newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian economy picks up, but rate cut on cards.
newsitem.headline: Australian economy picks up, but rate cut on cards.

text.p: Australia's brittle economy picked up slightly in the March quarter, according to data released on Wednesday, but the news failed to end hopes of another interest rate cut.

The economy grew by 0.9 percent in the three months, double the growth seen in the December quarter and within expectations, but annual growth for the year to March fell to 2.4 percent, the official data showed.
Year-on-year economic growth was 3.1 percent in March 1996.
"The Australian economy can afford to grow more quickly ands, as such, an easing of monetary policy is still likely," said Craig James, senior economist with Colonial State Bank.
The Australian dollar, which has been sliding on speculation of a fifth straight cut in the official cash interest rate, did not budge on the news.
Earlier in day, it breathed a small sigh of relief, rising against the U.S. dollar when Australia's central bank made no mention of a rate cut in its daily market briefing.
Wednesday's Australian Bureau of Statistics data also failed to shake the bond market's faith in another rate cut, with short-term market rates still trading below the 5.5 percent official cash rate.
Economists expect economic growth to pick up in the second half of calendar 1997 and have tipped growth to bounce back to around four percent for the fiscal year to June 30, 1998.
